slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: Mixed environments break on identity, not hardware

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Hardly any business runs on one platform only. Designers and developers want Macs, finance and operations are on Windows, and the two have to share the same files, the same email and the same security rules. When that goes wrong, it is almost never because the hardware cannot cope. It is because identity and file access were never joined up.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: The fix is to stop treating Macs as visitors on the network. Connect them to the same directory everyone else uses, so a Mac user signs in with the same Microsoft 365 account, the same multi-factor authentication applies, and revoking access when someone leaves genuinely revokes it everywhere.

slots.label: Heading 3
slots.default: Files, printing and the awkward bits

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Keep shared files in SharePoint and OneDrive rather than a legacy file share, which is where cross-platform setups usually start to creak. Then test the practical things on both platforms instead of assuming they work. Printing, VPN and conditional access are the usual culprits.

slots.label: Heading 4
slots.default: Handled by us, not a reseller chain

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: We are a Microsoft Cloud Solution Provider, so the Microsoft 365 and Entra ID side is handled directly by us rather than through a reseller chain, and the Mac side is managed to the same standard as the PCs beside it.
